niche: a branded tea maker choosing which deal mechanic to offer an Irish franchise symbol group's March 2027 central deal event, where each member store sets its own everyday prices and a featured line has to forecast at least two and a half times its base sales
stakeholder_role: revenue growth manager at a branded tea company

spine.entity: one franchise store's weekly sales of one tea line
spine.source: synthetic (fictional symbol group's category scan data); real Eircode routing keys and Irish public holidays

world.org_type: branded tea company selling through an Irish franchise symbol group

driver: A planned move earns a second response only at the points where its new level falls to or below a rival option's own level at that same point, a response visible exactly in the rival's volume during other subjects' moves; the subject's own closed moves never reached that level anywhere, so its own response curve reproduces its whole history and misses the plan, other subjects' curves that cross everywhere overstate it, and a crossing tested against the rival's average level misplaces it, because the rival's level differs point by point.
driver_concrete: Delahunt's 160s earns the own-label switch only in the stores where a mechanic puts its deal price at or below that store's own-label 160s price, which the own-label line's collapse during other brands' deep deals shows exactly; none of Delahunt's own deals ever went below own label, so its own curve says no mechanic clears the group's floor, the recap's mainstream lifts say Save a third clears it, the chain-average own-label price says only half price does, and the store-by-store test says Save 40% clears it inside the funding budget.
stump: A competent solver fits Delahunt's own deal lift from its Save 20% and Save 25% events, carries it to the four March mechanics, finds none reaches the group's two-and-a-half-times floor and advises sitting the event out (or, borrowing the recap's mainstream lifts, offers Save a third); the step that lands it there is never asking where the mainstream lines' extra deal volume came from, which the own-label 160s answers: its sales fell to three tenths of normal in exactly the store-weeks where a branded deal price sat at or below that store's own-label shelf price, and in the stores whose own-label price is highest Save 40% puts Delahunt there.
